sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Consumer Polling and Cross-Border Market Research Platform

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law governs Quebec private law (Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c CCQ-1991); Common Law governs federal, public, criminal, and tax law; bijural federal state.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-People's Republic of China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, signed 2012; in force 1 Oct 2014)
Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA, in force 1 Jul 2020)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP, in force for Canada 30 Dec 2018)
Canada-People's Republic of China Income Tax Agreement (DTA, signed 1986; in force 29 Dec 1986; QST/GST issues outside treaty scope)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184, as amended; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part XII.2; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Act), SC 2017, c 21; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1 (QBCA), including the register of individuals with significant control (25% ownership/control threshold); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (REQ registration and name-reservation regime); Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, CQLR c P-39.1 (Quebec Law 25) for panel data privacy governance.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access: the QBCA significant-control register is internal to the corporation; it is not publicly searchable, but must be disclosed to the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ), Revenu Quebec, the Autorite des marches financiers, FINTRAC, and law-enforcement bodies on lawful demand; nominee structures must be pierced for each 25%+ layer.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized true copy of Power of Attorney (procuration) appointing a Quebec-resident incorporation agent/mandataire
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the incorporator's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the country of issuance (in force for Canada since 11 Jan 2024); for non-Convention states, consular legalization by the Consulate General of Canada with jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copies of passport/photo ID and proof of residential address for each director, officer, and 25%+ UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization (as above)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency and corporate register excerpt, where a legal entity is a shareholder/director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the corporate shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; certified French translation required for REQ filings

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn UBO declaration and ownership-chain chart (source of funds and each significant-control link, 25%+ threshold)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; parallel internal QBCA register entry upon incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, 25%+ UBOs, and material counterparties against (i) the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions lists; (ii) Canadian regulations under SEMA, the United Nations Act, and the Magnitsky Act (including Russia, Belarus, Iran, Syria, Venezuela, and Haiti regimes); (iii) FINTRAC's politically-exposed-persons and heads-of-international-organizations framework, triggering enhanced due diligence when any PEP/HPIO is identified despite the Low_Risk_Standard tier; and (iv) prudent OFAC SDN-list screening because the PayPal Mass Payout and Wise rails are USD-denominated. All results must be documented in the pre-incorporation client-acceptance file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) online portal - Registre des entreprises (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); federal CBCA names instead use Corporations Canada's NUANS-based name-request service (https://www.ic.gc.ca/ccr) but the Quebec registration with REQ remains mandatory regardless of incorporation route.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and REQ name policy, a Quebec company's name must be in French or carry a French version; the legal element must be a French suffix (Societe par actions / S.A., Corporation / Corp., Limitee / Ltee, Incorporee / Inc.); Latin-script transliteration is required for names originating in non-Latin scripts; a numerical designation (e.g., 1234-5678 Quebec Inc.) is permissible in Quebec; English-only suffixes or English-only names are not registerable as the primary name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying financial institution or capital markets activity absent ministerial/AMF consent: Banque, Bank, Assurance, Insurance, Fiducie, Trust, Pret, Finance
Terms implying Crown, state, or regulatory authority: Canada, Quebec, Commission, Police, Ministere, Gendarmerie, Royal, Souvereign
Regulated professional titles absent professional-order consent: Avocat, Notaire, Medecin, Ingenieur, Comptable, Architecte, Courtier
Terms contrary to public order, morality, or obscene defamatory content
Registered trademarks or names confusingly similar to existing REQ or NUANS registrations without the owner's written consent
Unmodified generic descriptive terms lacking a distinctive element (e.g., 'Survey Platform' without an identifier)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon REQ name refusal (avis de refus), (1) the applicant files a written request for reconsideration (demande de revision) with the REQ within 30 days of the refusal notice, attaching consent letters, trademark registrations, or a revised distinct element; (2) if refused a second time, the applicant may either reserve a new name or file an application for judicial review (pourvoi en controle judiciaire) with the Cour superieure du Quebec within 60 days of the final decision (Code of Civil Procedure, c-25.01, arts. 529 ff.); (3) for trademark-based refusals, a concurrent consent letter or coexistence agreement is the fastest commercial remedy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with substance safeguards: the QBCA head office (siege social) must be a real physical address in Quebec where statutory records, the significant-control register, and service of process can be accessed; a P.O.-box-only or pure-shell virtual address is insufficient; a law-firm/service-provider office with mail forwarding and records custody is the market-standard solution for a low-risk market-research SaaS platform.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 3-5% annualized probability in the first three years for a non-regulated retail-market-research business); REQ does not conduct routine unannounced site inspections of low-risk service entities; FINTRAC/AMF inspection exposure is immaterial unless the PayPal Mass Payout/Wise flows develop into in-scope money-services activity; CRA / Revenu Quebec audits are desk-based and rarely involve physical premises checks.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: REQ name research and reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (Règlement sur les frais exigibles en vertu de la Loi sur la publicité légale des entreprises; approx. CAD 46)

Legal drafting and filing of QBCA articles of incorporation, organizational minutes, and minute-book setup

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Establishment of the QBCA register of individuals with significant control and UBO disclosure matrices
Notarization, Hague Apostille, and consular-legalization bundle for four KYC/origin documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local notarial tariff plus statutory apostille fee (approx. CAD 40 per document in Canada; foreign equivalents vary)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of constitutive and KYC documentation
Virtual head-office / service address and mail-forwarding (3 months)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, UN/Canadian/OFAC sanctions screening, and AML risk assessment report
Investment Canada Act notification filing (non-Canadian control of a new business)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm (Government of Canada filing fee: nil)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark (CAD 150-250) plus nil statutory filing fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for courier, bank-branch apostille duplicate, and miscellaneous disbursements

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c. S-31.1, ss. 6-24 (incorporation), ss. 29-38 (registered office and records), ss. 106-124 (directors and officers); Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, Part 1 (alternative federal route)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Direction de l'immatriculation
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation / Statuts de constitution (REQ Form 602) together with Registered Office and First Directors Declaration (REQ Form 603)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required under the QBCA; shares may be allotted without fully paid consideration upon written contract. No escrow account requirement for cash subscriptions; non-resident ownership permitted without capital escrow conditions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporator and initial directors hereby adopt the proposed Articles of Incorporation, accept the written subscriptions for one hundred (100) Class A common shares, and instruct the Secretary-Treasurer to file the Articles with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Corporation is hereby fixed at 1000 Rue de la Gauchetière Ouest, Montreal, Quebec H3B 4W5, and that the first directors shall adopt corporate bylaws consistent with the QBCA. RESOLVED FURTHER, that officers are appointed, banking authorizations are granted, and all statutory filings with Revenu Québec and the CRA are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Online Name Reservation Service / NUANS search system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name declaration request for a distinctive legal name with mandatory French-language component (e.g., 'ALPHA PANEL RECHERCHE INC.'). Confirm name availability through the NUANS report submitted by a licensed search house; ensure the proposed corporate name does not conflict with existing trademarks or legal persons registered in Quebec.
required_dossiers: Name declaration form (Demande de réservation de nom)
NUANS search report
Disponibilité and linguistic compliance attestation
Consent from the proposed director or legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name rejected or objected to, amend and resubmit the name declaration online; REQ grants 30 days for reconsideration. Alternatively, file a name rectification request under QBCA and attach a revised NUANS report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Québec Business Registry, Electronic Filing Portal (E-Services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Articles of Incorporation (Form 602) specifying the corporate name, share structure (Class A common shares, with or without stated value), restrictions on share transfers, number of directors, and the designated registered office address. Execute the articles by hand or via digital signature; upload the completed electronic form through REQ online, pay the incorporation tariff, and receive the certificate of incorporation (attestation de constitution).
required_dossiers: Completed and executed REQ Form 602 Articles of Incorporation
Name reservation certificate or NUANS report
Director consent forms (consentement du administrateur)
Registered office consent (formulaire de consentement du siège social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a query or notice of intended refusal, respond within 45 days with corrective documentation. Where the deficiency is fatal, file a rectificateur amendment (amending articles) with REQ or make a fresh filing without penalty. Any negative decision may be judicially reviewed before the Québec Superior Court pursuant to section 24 QBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Declaration of Registered Office and First Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Post-Incorporation Update / Déclaration de constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of the certificate of incorporation, file REQ Form 603 identifying the registered office address, the mailing address, the list of first directors with residential addresses and citizenship, and the officers (President, Secretary-Treasurer). This declaration constitutes the official record for corporate governance and initiates the annual registration update cycle.
required_dossiers: REQ Form 603 Declaration of Registered Office and First Directors
Certificate of incorporation number and date
Directors' physical address and contact details
Consent of each director to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late or erroneous declaration can be corrected by filing an updated declaration online; REQ imposes a late-filing penalty of up to C$300 per month. If declaration is rejected, resubmit with accurately notarized consents and proof of director identity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Adoption of Corporate Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (internal governance competence); document retention at registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting (in person or by teleconference) to adopt the pro-forma board resolution: confirm share subscriptions and issuance, appoint directors and officers, adopt the general corporate bylaws, approve the corporate seal and banking resolutions, and authorize the opening of operational bank accounts with PayPal Mass Payout and Wise. Minutes of the organizational meeting must be entered in the corporate records ledger.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first Board Resolution (approved minutes)
Bylaws of the Corporation (règlements administratifs)
Share subscription forms and issuance register
Bank account authorization resolutions
Corporate record book and seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the board cannot reach consensus on officer appointments, amend the resolution by a subsequent written resolution signed by the majority of directors; failure to minuting properly is cured by a retrospective directors' resolution and ledger entry under company records rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations with Revenu Québec and CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (Registre des entreprises), Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Number Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for Quebec employer accounts (QST and source deductions) and GST/HST account through Revenu Québec's 'Clic Revenu' portal or CRA's Business Registration Online; obtain a 16-digit Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and a federal 9-digit business number (BN). Election to have GST/HST and QST integrated is automatically applied in Quebec. Also register for the CNESST contribution account if any employees are hired, and obtain the duly filed attestation of suitability for holders of a permit under the Act respecting contracting by public bodies.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation (attestation de constitution)
NEQ number and BN confirmation
Directors' identification documents (ID, SIN optional)
Description of business activity ISIC 7320 / NAICS 541910
Estimated payroll and revenue details for quota and tax registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registrations are rejected or subject to administrative hold, correct the classification code (ISIC/NAICS) and re-submit through the REQ online portal; CRA and Revenu Québec provide a 30-day objection window. In case of duplicate NEQ/BN, call the joint registration helpline to merge the accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal and Occupational Health and Safety Compliance Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipalité de Montréal (Permis et licences); CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain any municipal occupancy permit for the leased office location through the Montreal 'Tout savoir sur mon dossier' portal if the building use changes or a new business category (information service) is registered; complete the CNESST establishment registration and display occupational health and safety posters. For an online survey platform operating with remote workers and a small administrative office, a physical industrial license is not required.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of registered office
CNESST establishment registration form (bir)
Fire safety inspection certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) issued by the municipal fire department
Certificate of building compliance / occupancy permit
Health and safety policy for remote workers and office personnel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality conditions the permit, cure by installing fire alarms, approved extinguishers, and illuminated exit signage; CNESST deficiencies are resolved through a corrective action plan filed on the CNESST portal within the imposed timeline. Appeals of CNESST orders may be lodged with the Administrative Labour Tribunal (TAT).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial or manufacturing license required for ISIC 7320 online consumer polling platform; only general business registration and occupational safety apply
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required; digital/IT service activity falls outside Quebec's industrial permit regime. If a local municipal 'business permit' is imposed, obtain a Ville de Montréal 'permis de commerce' for office-based information service activity only

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 1 (No EIA required) for non-industrial information technology and market research services; zero manufacturing emissions, no wastewater discharge, and minimal general office waste
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable: no point-source emissions. General environmental compliance via municipal waste collection, electronic waste recycling under Quebec's Règlement sur les halocarbures (if applicable) and federal Toxic Substances Management Policy; office generators or HVAC must comply with MELCCFP noise bylaws if installed (not expected).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Quebec Fire Safety Code (Building Act, c. B-1.1) required for the leased office; structural load inspection not applicable for an office-only tenancy; workplace health and safety clearance from CNESST required before onboarding staff, including a hazard prevention program (programme de prévention) if the employer has more than 20 employees, and annual inspection records for IT hardware and electrical installations; accessibility clearance under Quebécé's Act to secure handicapped persons' exercise of rights for public-facing premises if the office receives clients (otherwise exempt for virtual-only operations).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Agence du revenu du Canada) – federal GST/HST and corporate income tax; online portals: My Business Account (CRA) and GST/HST NETFILE. Quebec provincial counterpart: Revenu Québec (Québec Government) for QST – portal: Clic Revenu Québec / Mon dossier d'entreprise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business in Canada or Quebec must register for a Business Number (BN) with CRA, using Form RC66 or online GST/HST registration for non-residents. Revenu Québec issues a separate provincial tax number for QST upon registration; the BN and QST number are effective as of the first taxable supply, unless the small-supplier threshold is exceeded. No separate TIN is issued beyond the BN/QST registrant identifiers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not offer a U.S.-style check-the-box election. A corporation's resident status and entity-level taxation are determined by legal facts. Available statutory elections include section 216 for non-resident owners of Canadian rental or timber income, foreign-affiliate joint elections, and anti-hybrid mismatch documentation procedures under ITA sections 18.15, 18.16, and 20.33 (no elective mismatch treatment).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST and QST (structured VAT-type system; federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax, plus Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in the immediately preceding four calendar quarters; for Quebec QST, the same CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold applies to taxable supplies in Quebec or with a Quebec nexus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or continuous e-invoicing stamping regime. GST/HST returns and certain scheduled information must be filed electronically; QST returns are filed through Revenu Québec's accelerated digital services. E-invoicing may be issued in EDI/XML/PDF/JSON formats, and CRA requires adequate electronic record linking, but there is no centralized pre-clearance or digital stamping requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For a Canadian-registered market research SaaS platform, supplies of services made to a non-resident recipient are generally zero-rated under Part VII of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act if the services are performed outside Canada or are not performed in relation to Canadian real property or goods for use in Canada; the recipient must be resident outside Canada and the contract and delivery records must establish the offshore nature of the service supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A/B3 for goods; service contracts and transfer-of-funds records for SaaS exports)
Bill of Lading (for goods; for services, an executed service agreement or e-commerce transaction log from PayPal/Wise)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank/FTD record evidencing foreign-source payment and FX repatriation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess zero-rating within four years (or longer for misrepresentation); penalties include 25% of the net GST/HST amount falsely claimed, interest accruals, and penalties under Excise Tax Act sections 280 and 286 for knowingly false statements. Revenu Québec imposes similar QST reassessment and penalty rules, including fines and potential criminal prosecution for tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), as monetary authority and manager of the Exchange Fund Account held for the Minister of Finance; prudential regulation of banks and authorized foreign banks by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); cross-border transaction surveillance and AML/CFT reporting by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada has no exchange-control authority for private commercial payments since Canada accepted IMF Article VIII, Sections 2, 3, and 4 obligations effective 15 December 1952; the Foreign Exchange Control Act regime was abolished in 1951. No currency-licensing or central-bank prior-approval applies to current or capital-account remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is freely convertible under a floating exchange-rate regime. Canada fully complies with IMF Article VIII, so there are no restrictions on payments and transfers for current international transactions, no discriminatory currency arrangements, and no multiple-currency practices. Capital-account transactions are also unrestricted, subject to non-resident investment screening under the Investment Canada Act: establishment of a new Canadian business by a non-Canadian triggers a mandatory ISED notification within 30 days, and acquisitions of control of a Canadian business above the WTO review threshold (C$1.043 billion enterprise value in 2024; updated annually) require a net-benefit review. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted without prior approval, but must satisfy the solvency and retained-earnings (realizable value) tests of the Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c S-31.1) and the Canada Business Corporations Act. Dividends paid to non-residents are subject to 25% Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act, generally reduced to 15% (portfolio) or 5% (substantial holding) under the Canada–US tax treaty, 15%/5% under the Canada–France treaty, or comparable treaty relief; the payer must file NR4 information returns with the CRA. All transactions may be denominated in CAD or any convertible foreign currency at the corporation's option.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian law imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no fixed repatriation timeline for export proceeds or cross-border service revenue from market research, panelist data, or SaaS subscriptions. A Quebec corporation may freely retain foreign currency in non-resident or domestic foreign-currency bank accounts, convert receipts at commercial spot rates, apply them to payables, or hedge them. The only applicable constraint is transactional transparency: every international electronic funds transfer (IETF) of C$10,000 or more, or multiple transfers totaling C$10,000 within 24 consecutive hours, must be reported to FINTRAC by the financial intermediary under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; the corporate client is required to provide accurate remittance information on all wire instructions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: MEDIUM, subject to strict legal constraints and a ring-fenced treasury architecture. Offshore digital EMI platforms (Wise, formerly TransferWise; PayPal via its licensed PSP entities) offer excellent multi-currency payout functionality, rapid remote onboarding, and lower-value disbursement economics, but they are not Canadian Schedule I or Schedule II banks and do not carry CDIC deposit insurance. Legal constraints: (i) an offshore EMI may not take deposits in Canada as a bank; its balances are uninsured e-money claims, creating counterparty risk; (ii) any EMI that performs foreign exchange dealing or money transfer for Canadian-resident clients must be registered with FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA as a money services business (MSB), and if it carries on such services in Quebec it must obtain registration from the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) under the Act respecting money-services businesses; (iii) to avoid characterization of the platform itself as an MSB, the platform must not hold, direct, or control client funds as a payment intermediary; disbursements to panellists must be treated as the corporation's own principal payments for services rendered, executed by a licensed PSP as an agent; (iv) Wise and PayPal Mass Payout should be used only as disbursement rails funded on a just-in-time basis from a tier-1 Canadian bank operating account, never as primary treasury custody; (v) all PSP accounts must be onboarded in the legal name of the Quebec corporation, with executed terms, sanctions screening, and sub-processor privacy safeguards under Quebec Law 25 (Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector) for panellist data.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is legally permitted in Canada; no federal or Quebec statute requires directors to appear physically before a bank. FINTRAC's KYC regime expressly allows remote identity verification using advanced video-verification standards (e.g., liveness detection and document authentication). However, major Canadian banks apply risk-based internal policies: for a newly incorporated, non-operating Quebec business corporation with non-resident owners, they typically require (i) at least one Canadian-resident director or a Quebec-registered authorized signatory to complete a live virtual interview with the branch's commercial AML team; (ii) certified or original corporate documents and notarized ID for any foreign director/UBO, with apostille/consular legalization where the bank's policy demands; and (iii) documentation of a substantive business nexus in Quebec, since a registered-agent mailing address alone is insufficient. For a foreign director who cannot attend a virtual interview on a reliable basis, a fallback of in-person presentation at a Canadian embassy or at a corresponding branch of the same banking group outside Canada is generally accepted. In practice, the mandate should be structured as: one director or delegated officer resident in Canada completes the interview; foreign directors submit notarized identity and source-of-wealth dossiers; all signatories obtain individual electronic signatures through the bank's secure onboarding platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated Quebec private corporation with no operating history, minimal paid-up capital, and no credit file (shell/undercapitalization red flag)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified English/French copy of QBCA articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation, and enterprise registration from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ); register of directors and shareholders; complete organizational chart; board resolutions authorizing banking mandates and account signatories; three-year business plan and financial projections; executed client contracts, platform terms of use, and panellist acquisition plan; source-of-funds statement for the initial capital injection; proof of capital wiring from the beneficial owner's regulated bank; anticipated transaction volumes and average payout values.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership chain, foreign-resident directors, and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) located in multiple jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport and second government-issued photo ID for each director and UBO, certified/notarized and apostilled; beneficial-ownership declaration and corporate ownership-chain chart; tax residency certificates (CRA certificate of residence, Form NR301, or treaty equivalent); regulated-bank reference letters for each significant shareholder; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds questionnaires; CVs and professional background summaries for principals; results of sanctions/PEP/adverse-media screening via a recognized World-Check-class database; confirmation of no politically exposed persons or restricted-jurisdiction nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency inbound wires from unrelated corporate sponsors (market research clients) combined with mass outbound micro-payouts to consumer panellists (potential layering/structuring pattern)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements with sponsor clients and panellist terms of service; narrative compliance memorandum explaining the commercial model (B2B clients fund surveys; panellists receive compensation as principals, not as money-transfer beneficiaries); representative payout ledger and reconciliation sample; contractual AML/sanctions warranties from corporate clients; panellist identity and consent records consistent with Quebec privacy law; platform-level fraud and duplicate-identity detection controls; FINTRAC MSB-scoping memorandum demonstrating that the entity is not an unregistered money transmitter because it contracts directly with service-provider panellists and uses a licensed PSP only as payment agent; transaction-monitoring and sanctions-screening policy documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commingling risk: client-funded incentive pools and escrow-like balances sitting in a treasury operating account without segregation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow/agency agreements and trust-accounting ledger segregating client prepayments from own funds; separate sub-account or tier structure for client incentive liabilities; accounting policy memo under IFRS/ASPE treating client advances as contract liabilities; quarterly board-pack reporting to the bank on aggregate balances and encumbrances; legal opinion, if required, confirming that client prepayments are not deposit liabilities and no unauthorized deposit-taking occurs; caps on aggregate client funds held before onward disbursement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fraud and privacy exposure in mass consumer payouts (identity fraud, bot accounts, impersonation, duplicate panellist profiles)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: KYC and verification controls for corporate sponsor clients; device/IP fingerprinting, anti-bot, CAPTCHA, and duplicate-identity detection measures; panellist payment-method verification for PayPal/Wise accounts; geolocation and sanctions-jurisdiction blocking rules; dispute-resolution and refund policy; data-privacy impact assessment under Quebec Law 25; cyber-insurance and PSP liability coverage; audit trail and sample fraud-prevention reports shared with the bank on a confidential basis.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for non-resident capital injection: (1) Execute a written share subscription agreement and board resolution approving the issuance of common shares to the non-resident shareholder; if a shareholder loan is used, execute a promissory note with arm's-length interest and clearly severable terms. (2) Settlement must be initiated from the shareholder's regulated bank account via SWIFT MT103 into the Quebec corporation's CAD-denominated tier-1 operating account (National Bank, RBC, or TD), with remittance information specifying: remitter legal name and UBO, purpose 'Inbound direct investment / share subscription', and reference to the subscription agreement number; USD or EUR funds may instead be wired to a foreign-currency account and converted by the Canadian bank's spot desk. (3) Canadian large-value clearing occurs over Payments Canada's Lynx system (formerly LVTS) for same-day final settlement of CAD wires. (4) Compliance checkpoints: file an Investment Canada Act 'Notification of Establishment of a New Canadian Business' with ISED within 30 days of the new Quebec business establishment if the direct owner is a non-Canadian; confirm Statistics Canada Balance of Payments direct-investment reporting obligations; the receiving financial institution will report an IETF of C$10,000 or more to FINTRAC and may require a source-of-wealth questionnaire. (5) Loan principal repayments and interest to non-residents are subject to Part XIII withholding (25%, reduced by treaty) unless an exemption applies; interest paid at arm's length to a non-resident lender generally qualifies for the Canadian 'fully exempt interest' provisions under the Income Tax Act and must be reported on Form 105 / NR4 if withheld. (6) Maintain strict separation between the capital/operating treasury account and panellist-liability sub-ledgers. (7) Complete the bank's standard incoming-transfer attestation, including confirmation that the funds do not originate from restricted jurisdictions and that all final beneficiaries are identified.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Recommended clearing-rail architecture for the ISIC 7320 market-research SaaS treasury: (a) SWIFT MT103 is the primary rail for vendor invoices, contractor settlements, intercompany payments, and any disbursement above C$10,000; wires are initiated via the bank's electronic banking channel and clear same-day across Lynx for CAD legs and via correspondent networks for USD/EUR legs; payment must carry a correct customer-reference and beneficiary-account identifiers. (b) Commercial letters of credit are not standard for data-driven services in this scope; documentary credit discipline is justified only for high-value international data-supply contracts, in which case use irrevocable LCs issued on SWIFT MT700 and confirmed/advised per UCP600. (c) For consumer panellist incentives, PayPal Mass Payout API is the preferred multi-country rail: it supports high-fan-out micro-payments and converts CAD at PayPal's applicable FX rates; treasury should pre-fund PayPal via ACH/EFT or SWIFT in small tranches from the Canadian operating account. (d) Wise (multi-currency account) serves as a secondary low-value cross-border rail using local clearing rails and mid-market FX, funded just-in-time to limit uninsured e-money exposure above operational needs. (e) Establish a monthly settlement cadence (e.g., net monthly disbursement cycle) to minimize between-currency conversion frequency; hold both CAD and USD operating accounts to absorb US-dollar client payments naturally. (f) Every outward international EFT of C$10,000 or more triggers FINTRAC IETF reporting by the financial institution; the corporation must maintain complete panellist/vendor records for audit. (g) Non-resident panellist payments are not subject to Canadian Part XIII withholding where the panelist performs services entirely outside Canada and no employment relationship exists; nevertheless, obtain W-8BENE/W-8BEN evidence, avoid intra-group management/technical service fees without transfer-pricing documentation, and confirm Quebec QST/GST treatment (zero-rated export supplies where the recipient is a non-resident and the service is performed for use outside Canada, with careful application of the place-of-supply rules under Excise Tax Act and Quebec Taxation Act harmonization).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP) up to 12 months with the tier-1 Canadian bank under an ISDA/CSA master agreement or the bank's standard commercial FX contract; requires a board resolution and a named treasury mandate; suitable for locking in sponsor-client receivable currency

FX swaps (spot-versus-forward matched legs) for intra-period liquidity bridging on settlement dates; permissible with Schedule I banks and useful for managing payout-timing mismatches without extending net exposure

Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD) permitted for long-term balance-sheet hedging, but proportionate only where intercompany debt or a material multi-year USD receivable exists; requires ISDA documentation and prudent valuation policy

Vanilla FX options (CAD put / USD call and USD call / CAD put) purchased from bank counterparties, limited to documented commercial exposure and subject to a no-leverage policy; premiums recognized as period costs

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible for settling exposures in restricted or low-liquidity currencies that arise from international panellist payouts in certain EMEA/Asia jurisdictions; CAD/USD itself is fully deliverable, so NDFs are never used for the core pair

Prohibited or restricted instruments: speculative leveraged OTC derivatives, binary options, cryptocurrency-based swaps, and any hedging without a corresponding forecast commercial exposure; all derivative transactions must be documented, marked-to-market monthly, and reported to the bank's treasury surveillance unit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Update (Mise à jour annuelle) of the enterprise registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Revenu Québec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each registration anniversary date under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 32 plus interest; failure to file for two consecutive years is a statutory ground for administrative dissolution (strike-off) by the Registraire.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership transparency declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires ultimes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same 60-day anniversary window as the annual update; filed every calendar year with any shareholding changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 7,500 for a legal person; the Registraire may refuse to issue attestations, publish the default, and dissolve the enterprise for repeated failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual registration fee of the enterprise (Droits annuels) for legal publicity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec / Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually after the Registraire issues the fee notice; aligned with the registration anniversary and due within the grace period stated on the notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest and late-payment penalty on the unpaid fee; persistent non-payment for two consecutive years may trigger administrative deregistration or dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal annual return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (applicable if the corporation is federally incorporated and registered extra-provincially in Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100; failure to file for at least three consecutive years permits the Director to dissolve the corporation under section 212 of the CBCA.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under QBCA section 216, an independent audit may be dispensed with for a non-reporting corporation having fewer than 16 shareholders and annual revenue below CAD 500,000 in the most recent fiscal year or in the two immediately preceding fiscal years; member approval and an annual written exemption resolution are required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is the default framework for a private Quebec business corporation; IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises and available by election; compiled financial statements are permitted below the audit threshold.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec's Transparency of Enterprises Act and QBCA require an annual declaration identifying every individual holding, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of the shares, votes, or economic rights of the corporation. Any share transfer creating a new qualifying beneficial owner between annual cycles must be recorded immediately in the internal register and reflected in the next annual transparency declaration; a written confirmation resolution must be adopted annually.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 - 450 per year (CAD 175 - 600) for a registered office or corporate agent service in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 - 6,500 per audit (CAD 2,500 - 8,000) for a typical SME market-research corporation, depending on transaction volume and statement complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal 15% + Quebec 11.5% = 26.5% combined general corporate rate (before credits)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction: federal 9% and Quebec 3.2% (combined ~12.2%) on first CAD 500,000 of active business income for Canadian-controlled private corporations; SR&ED investment tax credit up to 35% on qualified R&D expenditures; Quebec Innovation and Productivity Tax Credit; patent box regime; foreign tax credits; notional interest deduction on equity in certain cases.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return – filed under the Income Tax Act via CRA My Business Account, approved tax software (NETFILE for corporations) or paper. Quebec CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return – filed via Revenu Québec's online portal for businesses (Cl@S or approved E-file).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal period cannot exceed 53 weeks; interim installments due quarterly for estimated current-year tax)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 and CO-17 must be filed within six months after fiscal year-end. Balance of tax payable due within two months of fiscal year-end for non-CCPCs, or three months for qualifying CCPC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the panel survey platform's income or loss from its Canadian sole activity, including SaaS subscription fees and cross-border payment processing revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporation filing T2 reports only income attributable to the business carried on in Canada; source revenues from Canadian survey panels must be allocated on a reasonable basis, typically using the income method under the tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim a credit for foreign income taxes paid on profits derived outside Canada, if any.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only available to Canadian-resident corporations; a non-resident corporation cannot claim foreign tax credits on Canadian T2, but may deduct excess foreign taxes as an expense in computing Canadian taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute taxable income after deductions and loss carryovers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation must compute taxable income on Part I income that is earned from carrying on business in Canada; do not include foreign-source income unless specifically taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CO-17: Line 330 (L'impôt calculé) / Quebec tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute Quebec provincial income tax on the corporation's Quebec taxable income, applying the 11.5% general rate or reduced small business rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must file CO-17 to report Quebec-source business income if they were carrying on business in Quebec; allocate Quebec taxable income using the Quebec allocation rules and any federal-provincial tax agreement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for each month of delinquency up to 12 months (maximum 17%); a minimum penalty of $100 may apply; repeat failure penalty doubles. Quebec imposes an analogous penalty under the Taxation Act. If the return is filed more than one year late, the federal penalty is 5% plus 1% per month up to 12. Interest accrues at prescribed rates. Non-resident corporations also face penalties and possible revocation of business registration.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (on dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to non-residents), subject to DTA reduction (e.g., 5% on DTA treaty dividends for 10%+ ownership; 15% portfolio dividends).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA, the non-resident recipient must obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority (e.g., IRS Form 6166 in the U.S.). The TRC is provided to the Canadian payer before the dividend payment; the payer may apply the reduced rate at source only if satisfied of beneficial ownership. Where tax was withheld at 25%, a refund claim is made by filing Form NR301 with CRA within two years of payment. The payer must retain the TRC and a completed RC4651 (if applicable) as part of the audit file. Without the TRC and beneficial ownership proof, WHT remains 25%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT for royalties and interest paid by a Canadian resident to a non-resident is 25%. Under DTAs, the rate is generally reduced to 0%-10% for interest (e.g., 10% to a U.S. interest recipient, 0% if arm's length), and royalties 10% (0% for copyright or cross-licensing in some treaties). Quebec does not levy a separate dividend WHT; the federal Part XIII and DTA apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A T106 information return and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation must be prepared when a taxpayer has transactions with a non-arm's length non-resident and the total aggregate value of such transactions exceeds CAD 1 million in the taxation year. However, CRA may request documentation for smaller transactions if required; a de facto threshold of CAD 1 million is frequently used as a safe-harbor.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no statutory Economic Substance Regulations similar to Caribbean regimes, but it applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under s.245 ITA and Quebec's anti-avoidance rules under the Taxation Act. CRA and Revenu Québec disregard transactions that have no legitimate business purpose and recharacterize the profit flow. A pure shell entity with no substance in a no-tax jurisdiction will be ignored, and its principal/controller will be taxed as having received the income directly.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly making false or misleading statements in T2/CO-17, understating subscription revenue from the survey platform, or maintaining a second set of books for payments received via PayPal/Wise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Income Tax Act s.239 and Quebec Taxation Act, criminal fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to five years; civil gross negligence penalty of 50% of understated tax; interest and arrears.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and controllers who authorized or consented to the false filings are personally liable as co-perpetrators; personal bank accounts can be seized, passports canceled and travel bans imposed, and imprisonment served.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a zero-tax Cayman or BVI shell to receive the Canadian platform's SaaS and survey revenue, while the Canadian entity performs all material functions and bears economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment denying the tax benefit and imposing a penalty of 50% of the tax benefit; Quebec's equivalent penalties apply; recharacterization of the shell's contracts and invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for the tax benefit if they signed statutory declarations or knew of the artificial structure; civil restitution orders, asset freezes, and potential director criminal liability for fraud if steps were executed without substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare transfer pricing documentation, or setting intercompany royalty/fee for the consumer panel data at a price not at arm's length with the foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: s.247(3) ITA penalty of 10% of the net transfer pricing adjustment plus interest; adjustment to taxable income; loss of deductions; additional provincial reassessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved false intercompany pricing may be found jointly responsible for the corporate tax debt if they signed the declaration of compliance; personal liability for unpaid source deductions is common, and TP penalties can be converted into a director assessment under wilful blindness.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the survey platform to launder funds by paying panelists with synthetic identities or knowingly accepting proceeds of crime from sponsors in violation of PCMLTFA; failing to register as a money services business when performing remittance-like functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PCMLTFA administrative penalties up to CAD 500,000 for corporations and CAD 100,000 per officer; criminal money laundering under Criminal Code s.462.31: imprisonment up to 10 years; asset forfeiture; potential revocation of the Quebec enterprise registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally prosecuted for money laundering if they knew of the illicit flow and derived benefit; convictions lead to travel bans, restitution orders, and imprisonment; personal assets are included in the criminal asset forfeiture process.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the T2 and CO-17 by the six-month deadline, or persistent failure to pay quarterly instalments for the survey platform's tax balance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalty (5% + monthly 1% up to 12 months) and the 50% gross negligence penalty; interest at prescribed rates; for repeated non-filing, Information Return penalties up to CAD 7,500 (not filed after demand) each.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a non-filing corporation are jointly and severally liable for any unremitted source deductions or GST/HST; they may be assessed personally under s.227.1 and equivalent Quebec provisions, and may be subject to travel bans under CRA collection enforcement.
